cosy-lesson.title: "Never confuse education with intelligence.": Richard Feynman

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Confuse – to fail to distinguish between two different things, thinking they are the same.

p.em: Example: People often confuse having many academic credentials with possessing deep wisdom.

cosy-blockquote.p: Credential – a qualification, certificate, or degree showing a person's educational background.

p.em: Example: He got the job because of his impressive credential, but he struggled with basic tasks.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intelligence – the real-world capacity to acquire knowledge, think logically, and solve complex problems.

p.em: Example: Street-smart survival requires a highly practical type of intelligence.

cosy-blockquote.p: Practical – concerned with the actual application of ideas and hands-on doing rather than theory.

p.em: Example: He had excellent practical experience, making him much faster at fixing machines.

cosy-blockquote.p: Theoretical – concerned with ideas, abstract concepts, or theories rather than practical use.

p.em: Example: School focus was too theoretical, making it difficult to understand how things work in reality.

cosy-blockquote.p: Autodidact – a self-taught person who acquires knowledge independently without formal teachers.

p.em: Example: As a passionate autodidact, she learned coding completely from books and free tutorials.

cosy-blockquote.p: Memorize – to commit something to memory exactly, often without understanding its real meaning.

p.em: Example: Students are pressured to memorize formulas just to pass their final exams.

cosy-blockquote.p: Understanding – a real, deep comprehension of how something works and why it behaves that way.

p.em: Example: Feynman said that knowing the name of a bird is completely different from real understanding.

cosy-blockquote.p: Curiosity – a strong, passionate desire to learn, know, or investigate simple and complex things.

p.em: Example: His relentless curiosity drove him to take apart old clocks to see how they worked.

cosy-blockquote.p: Grades – the marks or scores given to students to evaluate their coursework and tests.

p.em: Example: High grades do not guarantee that a student is capable of thinking independently.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why do people so often confuse being highly educated with being highly intelligent?
★ Have you ever met someone who had an impressive credential but lacked basic common sense?

How does Feynman's quote challenge our traditional definition of human intelligence?
★ Do you believe that your own intelligence is mostly practical or highly theoretical?

What is the danger of relying purely on a theoretical education without any hands-on practice?
★ In your career or studies, do you prefer practical tasks or reading about theories?

How does a successful autodidact differ from a person who only learns inside a classroom?
★ Have you ever tried to study a completely new language or skill as an autodidact?

Why do traditional school systems force students to memorize information instead of encouraging critical thinking?
★ Was it easy for you to memorize historical dates and formulas during your school years?

What is the difference between simply knowing the name of a concept and having a deep understanding of it?
★ Can you share a topic where you have a genuine, passionate understanding?

How can parents and teachers keep a child's natural curiosity alive within a strict schooling system?
★ What subject sparked your greatest curiosity when you were a teenager?

Do school grades accurately reflect a student's real capabilities and intelligence?
★ Did you care a lot about your academic grades when you were in school?

How does having a prestigious academic credential affect a person's intellectual humility?
★ Do you find it easy to admit your ignorance when discussing complex subjects with experts?

Why did Feynman believe that playing and experimenting is essential to acquiring real understanding?
★ What is the most fun, playful experiment or project you have done recently?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: In which scenario is a theoretical education least helpful? Rank them from most to least dependent on formal schooling: - 💼 Running a Business Managing practical risks, negotiating, and solving unexpected crisis situations under pressure. - 🎻 Creating Original Art Developing genuine creative expression, playing with style, and making emotional connections. - 🚀 Writing Smart Code Designing robust database logic, debugging algorithms, and acting as an autodidact developer. - 🔬 Doing Academic Research Studying highly complex theoretical papers and cataloging research credentials for scientific review.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, standard academic grades will be completely replaced by dynamic portfolio metrics. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be happier if future schools stopped using any numerical grades to evaluate children?

Future recruitment algorithms will never confuse a high-prestige degree with genuine, practical intelligence. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you trust an automated AI agent to assess your raw intelligence during an interview?

With the rise of instant neural memory transfers, nobody will ever have to memorize any facts or vocabulary again. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could instantly memorize any book, would you miss the struggle of learning?

The most successful professionals of the next decades will all be self-guided autodidact specialists rather than traditional students. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you hope to remain an active, passionate autodidact for the rest of your life?

As AI tutors personalize all education, every child will cultivate their natural curiosity instead of conforming to standard curriculums. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you had a personal AI tutor, what topic would you explore to feed your curiosity?

In an automated world, holding a theoretical credential will carry zero value in the labor market. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you want your children to chase a formal credential just to ensure their social safety?

Future virtual simulations will make practical training so perfect that traditional apprenticeships will disappear. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you feel comfortable hiring a self-taught mechanic who only has practical VR training?

The hyper-academic focus of future societies will leave no room for the playful, simple understanding that Feynman championed. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What is the most important lesson about building simple, clear understanding that you want to pass on?

A future world with instant search logic will make our formal, theoretical study of history and science completely redundant. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you believe that reading heavy, theoretical philosophy will always remain valuable?

As society becomes more automated, the choice to learn will be driven purely by a lifelong desire to satisfy our minds. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What is one complex skill you hope to master as part of your lifelong self-development?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am agree with Feynman → Correct: I agree with Feynman ((Agree is a verb and does not use 'am'))
Incorrect: He explained me the problem → Correct: He explained the problem to me ((Explain + object + 'to' + person))
Incorrect: I've been in school since 10 years → Correct: I've been in school for 10 years ((Use 'for' for duration))
Incorrect: Feynman makes us to think → Correct: Feynman makes us think ((Make + object + bare infinitive))
